_README: The private protocol: a compile database SUPERSET. It is the ONE artifact the
onboarding skill produces, and the only thing the flow reads about a project's
build. The skill's job is to FILL THIS TEMPLATE IN: everything the shape can
express is here; the skill supplies the corpus's values.
WHY A SUPERSET. A compile database says how each translation unit is compiled
and nothing else: not which units link into which product, not which module a
unit defines, not which sources the build has to GENERATE first, not how the
project is PATCHED, OVERLAID or CONFIGURED before it can build at all. Without
these a build cannot be produced from the file. So they are recorded here,
once, by the skill that had the real build in front of it.
EVERY SECTION IS ALWAYS PRESENT. A section with nothing to say is `[]` (or an
object with empty fields), never omitted: the shape is the contract, and a
section that appears only when a corpus happens to use it makes two corpora
produce two different shapes for the same kind of fact -- a consumer cannot
tell 'this corpus has none' from 'this reader did not look'.
TWO SPELLINGS OF A PATH, load-bearing:
* a path UNDER `${TREE}` is one the replay must MAKE for itself (generated
sources, objects) -- it travels with the protocol;
* a path that is ABSOLUTE is one the replay READS (the project's own sources
do not move) -- it does not travel and must not be rewritten.
`$` is reserved: a literal dollar is `$$`; a bare `$` is malformed and refused.
THE KEY IS THE STEM, not a file name: removing ONE trailing extension and
keeping case is what makes `isamax.f` and `isamax.cpp` one unit and one link
member.
_protocol_version: The only version this consumer reads. A file from another version is refused, not coerced.
_comment: Free text. Says where this came from, for a human reading it later.

_README: WHERE the protocol was captured from, and what that tree IS. The onboard
skill observes this from the build; it is not derived later, because a
wrong guess resolves `${TREE}` to the wrong directory and every generated
source then names a file that does not exist.
capture._tree: What `${TREE}` denotes for this protocol -- the tree the build RAN in. For an out-of-source build that is the build directory (`.../build`), not the source checkout beside it; the two differ by a level and the difference silently changes where every generated source lands.
capture._layout: 'in_source' or 'out_of_source'. Whether the build ran IN the corpus's source tree or in a separate build directory. Recorded so a consumer reproduces the same tree, not a similar one.

_README: One entry per translation unit. The first four fields are the standard
compile-database fields, unchanged, so a cc-only consumer works. This
example defines BOTH stems the `products` below reference, so the
template is a protocol the mechanism accepts.
compilation._directory: The directory the command ran in. Relative path operands in `command` are relative to THIS.
compilation._command: EXACTLY what the project's own build ran, re-rooted at `${TREE}`. This is the authority on the unit's flags.
compilation._file: The unit's source. Under `${TREE}` when the build GENERATED it; absolute when the project ships it.
compilation._output: The object the command produces, as the build spelled it.
compilation._stem: The unit's extension-independent identity, and the protocol's KEY. A product's members are stems.
compilation._variant: 'fortran' or 'cpp' -- which form of this stem this entry describes.
compilation._provides: Fortran modules this unit DEFINES, lowercased. Omitted when empty (still a valid entry).
compilation._uses: Fortran modules this unit USES, lowercased. Omitted when empty.
compilation._preprocess: The PREPROCESS step, when the build has one. DEFINES go here and only here. Omitted when the build has no separate preprocess step.

_README: Sources the build MAKES before it can compile anything. A replay that
names one without a rule to produce it fails on one missing file among
thousands. Empty `[]` when the build generates nothing.
generated_inputs._output: The file this rule produces. Under `${TREE}`, always.
generated_inputs._command: A SHELL LINE, not an argv list. Run it through a shell; do not split or re-quote it.
generated_inputs._depends: What must exist to run the rule, in the build's own order.

_README: What the build links. Members/objects are STEMS defined in `compilation`,
so the link line follows a unit from one form to the other.
products._members: For an 'archive': the STEMS that go into it.

products._objects: For an 'exe': the STEMS of its own translation units.
products._libs: For an 'exe': libraries it links, IN ORDER (`ld` resolves left to right).
products._driver: The command used to link. Omitted when the build's own link line is not needed.
products._flags: Link-time flags, when the recorded link line had any. Omitted when empty.

_own_roots: The directories (tree-relative) that are the corpus's OWN units, when its build pulls in third-party subprojects it should NOT convert. Empty `[]` means every compiled unit is the corpus's own.

_README: Infrastructure the corpus needs ONCE, for the repeated builds and runs
that follow: a `git submodule` fetch, a portability patch, an overlay
copy, a configure step. Each entry carries a CHECK -- the corpus's own
way of telling it is already done -- so it runs AT MOST ONCE and a
repeat is a no-op ('the submodule is already there, do not re-fetch').
That is what lets a rebuild start from a raw checkout without paying
for the setup every time. Empty `[]` when the corpus needs none.
prepare._check: How to know this is ALREADY done, as a predicate over the tree. A `path` that must EXIST (with `exists: true`, the default) or must be ABSENT (`exists: false`, e.g. a marker a patch writes). When it holds, the step is SKIPPED.
prepare._run: The command to run when the check does not hold. A shell line.

_README: Build facts a compile database cannot carry: which optimization level the
CONVERTED C++ is built at (which can differ from the source's), the policy
flags every unit gets, and the extra include/module directories the build
exports.

flags._optimize: A map from the SOURCE command's optimization token to the one the CONVERTED code must use. Empty `{}` keeps the source's level. A corpus whose own CMake lowers its Fortran from -O3 to -O2 needs this; one that does not leaves it empty.
flags._policy: Flags applied to every unit, independent of the recorded command.

build._module_dirs: Tree-relative directories the build writes Fortran `.mod` files into. Empty when the corpus declares none.
build._include_dirs: Tree-relative include directories the build exports. Empty when none.

_README: Tests the build system REGISTERED, as the build system itself reports
them. Empty `[]` when the project registers none; a corpus with a
registered suite is self-verifying and needs no stored golden.
tests.name: Suite_Summary
tests._depends: The registered test names this one runs after, in the build's order.
tests._working_directory: Where the test command runs, when the build says so. Omitted when it runs at the build root.

_README: Files a run READS that are not sources and not generated -- a validation
input template, a resource. Recorded because a replay outside the capture
tree would otherwise look for them and not find them. Empty `[]` when none.
support_files._content: The file's contents, so the replay can recreate it.
